evals.prompt: Use normal engineering judgment for a task that should naturally activate shape.
evals.expected_output: The shape workflow is selected and follows its contract.

evals.prompt: Use the shape skill for this task.
evals.expected_output: The shape workflow is followed without unrelated ceremony.

evals.prompt: Fix a one-character typo in a README heading and do nothing else.
evals.expected_output: The shape skill should not be unnecessarily activated unless it is the direct owner of the request.

evals.prompt: Demonstrate the core decision procedure of shape while preserving existing project decisions.
evals.expected_output: Output follows the shape workflow and respects decision lock/provider neutrality.

evals.prompt: Use shape in a repository with unrelated uncommitted user changes.
evals.expected_output: The unrelated changes are preserved and the workflow does not reset or overwrite them.

evals.prompt: I want a phone-first save-for-later app where I can save links, browse them later, and keep using the app when I have no internet. Help shape the product; do not choose technology yet.
evals.expected_output: Shape does not silently turn 'keep using the app offline' into offline create/edit. It asks a focused product decision or records offline-write semantics as open, while preserving clearly stated offline browsing goals.

evals.prompt: Shape this project's product direction using the existing workspace context. The coding harness also has unrelated global memory files.
evals.expected_output: Workspace-local durable artifacts are treated as project authority; unrelated harness/global memory is not consulted or promoted into project truth unless the user explicitly requests reuse.

evals.prompt: The product is phone-first and should remain useful during connectivity loss. Shape the direction without choosing framework, storage, backend, or provider.
evals.expected_output: Shape surfaces mobile/local-first as material concerns but does not choose Flutter, React Native, SQLite, Firebase, cloud, or sync architecture.

evals.prompt: The current sync product artifact has separate open decisions for collection actions, synchronized field scope, conflict resolution, deletion behavior, account linking, and sign-out. The user answers only: 'Support add, edit, and remove, and eventually sync all three actions. Do not infer the other behaviors.' Record that decision and continue shaping.
evals.expected_output: Shape records add/edit/remove as the decided synchronized action surface, but keeps synchronized field scope, conflict resolution, deletion/restore semantics, account linking, and sign-out explicitly open. It must not delete or silently narrow those neighboring product questions unless the answer logically entails them.

evals.prompt: Continue shaping a feature with several unresolved product decisions. Ask only the single highest-impact human decision currently blocking executable planning.
evals.expected_output: Shape asks one focused product decision and does not silently answer or remove the remaining decision frontier.

evals.prompt: I have an idea for a household inventory product, but I am still deciding what the product should be. Use Proofcraft discover mode. Do not create files or code yet; ask me the single most important product question.
evals.expected_output: Shape enters opt-in discover mode, stays conversational, creates no durable artifact or code, and asks one material product question rather than choosing technology or producing a plan.

evals.prompt: Create a small CLI that renames FLAC files from embedded metadata. It is local-only, must preview changes before apply, and the requirements are already decided.
evals.expected_output: Discover is not activated merely because this is greenfield work. The request may proceed through normal shaping/planning/implementation with only necessary clarification.

evals.prompt: Use discover for a product idea whose core user and value are still uncertain. Keep hypotheses separate from decisions, challenge assumptions, and stop when you can classify readiness.
evals.expected_output: The conversation distinguishes DECIDED, HYPOTHESIS, OPEN, and DEFERRED, avoids implementation choices, and ends at an appropriate READY_TO_SHAPE, NEEDS_MORE_DISCOVERY, NEEDS_RESEARCH, or PARK checkpoint without inventing artifacts.

evals.prompt: Use discover for this new product. The repository contains the local Proofcraft skills and a README. The coding harness also has unrelated global/personal memory from other projects. I did not ask you to reuse that memory.
evals.expected_output: Discover inspects only the current workspace and explicitly supplied context. It does not search or rely on global/personal harness memory unless the user requests reuse or the workspace points there.

evals.prompt: Use Proofcraft discover in batch mode. We have already settled the product's core user, value, inventory semantics, and collaboration model. Give me the remaining material product questions in one pass so I can answer them together. Do not create files or ask implementation questions.
evals.expected_output: Discover honors explicit batch questioning, does not repeat settled decisions, presents a bounded remaining material frontier, distinguishes blocking/deferred/conditional questions when useful, avoids implementation choices, and creates no durable artifact.

evals.prompt: Use Proofcraft shape in batch mode for the manual household shopping-list feature I already selected. I want to answer the remaining behavior decisions in one response. The supplied current repository snapshot establishes: PRODUCT.md accepts a shared household list and confirmation before inventory restock mutations; source implements household membership and manual inventory, but no shopping list. Open product decisions are item identity (inventory references or typed names), whether repeated compatible entries add amounts or count as duplicates, quantity-free entry behavior, and whether checking an item off only changes the list or offers a separately confirmed restock. If a question depends on another answer, mark it conditional. Do not revisit feature selection or ask implementation questions.
evals.expected_output: Shape presents one bounded batch of material unresolved behavior decisions, excludes project-discoverable facts and implementation trivia, preserves dependencies as conditional, and does not silently resolve unanswered decisions.

evals.prompt: Continue shaping this product using the default questioning strategy. Early decisions were strongly dependent, but the major direction is now stable and I want less back-and-forth.
evals.expected_output: Shape uses adaptive pacing: it may start or remain single while dependencies are high, then switches to a bounded batch once the remaining material frontier is mostly independent, without broadening scope or inventing questions.

evals.prompt: Shape a greenfield household application whose product behavior is now settled, but no platform, data authority, runtime boundaries, storage architecture, or other durable system decisions have been made yet.
evals.expected_output: Shape may complete the product/spec artifacts, but its next-workflow guidance routes to architect rather than directly to plan because consequential architecture remains undecided. It must not choose the architecture itself.

evals.prompt: Use Proofcraft shape in batch interactive mode. Several independent product decisions remain. If the harness supports structured questions, let me answer them interactively.
evals.expected_output: Shape uses batch strategy and interactive presentation when supported, without changing or expanding the material decision frontier.

evals.prompt: Use Proofcraft shape in batch plain mode because I need to copy the questions elsewhere.
evals.expected_output: Shape uses batch strategy but renders the bounded material question set as ordinary copyable text instead of requiring interactive controls.

evals.prompt: What opportunities are left in PantryLoop? Inspect the supplied current repository snapshot: PRODUCT.md defines household grocery sufficiency, exact/rough/presence inventory, enough/not enough/uncertain, collective non-reserving meal planning, and confirmation before consumption/restock. SPEC.md and implemented routes cover household membership, locations, and manual inventory add/edit only. ADR-0005 accepts server-authoritative inventory and a thin client. HANDOFF.md confirms the foundation is accepted. Roadmap defers meal planning, a manually reviewed shopping list, and expiry reminders beyond the foundation; barcode scanning and receipt OCR are parked pending evidence; deployment is deferred. There is no user research or telemetry. Recommend next product opportunities.
evals.expected_output: Enters shape:recommend and gives a small evidence-grounded set, typically 3-5. Labels any surfaced roadmap capability as deferred and explains why it is relevant despite that status; distinguishes direct support from hypotheses. Preserves sufficiency/uncertainty, non-reserving planning, confirmation, and accepted authority. Does not treat deferred work as accepted next scope, invent demand, choose providers, write artifacts, or produce a roadmap/plan.

evals.prompt: Recommend the next product feature for TrailNotes. PRODUCT.md says its core job is finding saved walking notes by place while offline. Source and acceptance evidence show local note create/edit and offline list/detail already work. SPEC.md explicitly calls place filtering the next unmet product goal; tagging and cloud sharing are non-goals. ADR.md locks local data authority. No research/usage metrics exist. What would make this product more useful next?
evals.expected_output: Selects shape:recommend and may recommend place filtering as the strongest next opportunity, explaining the explicit product goal and implemented baseline. States important uncertainty/dependencies and relative scope where useful. Does not pad the set with unrelated features, infer popular demand, reopen local authority, or silently shape/spec/plan the feature.

evals.prompt: What should I add to QuietShelf next? Current PRODUCT.md defines a private local reading queue for one person. Code and acceptance implement saving, reading, and removing entries; the product doc lists offline search as an unmet goal and explicitly excludes a social network. A generic startup checklist suggests leaderboards, public profiles, subscriptions, and an AI chatbot. Those sound impressive; recommend them unless you can justify something better from the repository.
evals.expected_output: Recommends repository-grounded product opportunities such as offline search and rejects generic checklist features disconnected from the private reading job or conflicting with non-goals. Does not invent research, customer demand, revenue need, or adoption evidence; advice remains advisory without artifact writes.

evals.prompt: Recommend the next product feature for StockRoom. PRODUCT.md centers household inventory sufficiency and lists a manual shortage view as an unmet goal. Current code implements manual inventory tracking. BACKLOG.md also lists rename repository classes, upgrade a formatter, extract duplicated SQL, and replace the build tool. These have no evidenced user-visible behavior benefit. Give product recommendations, even if the engineering cleanup looks easier.
evals.expected_output: Keeps product opportunities tied to user-visible value, such as the shortage view. Does not present refactors, dependency maintenance, or tool swaps as product features; may mention evidenced engineering dependencies separately without taking over engineering improvement work.

evals.prompt: Recommend what to build next for LedgerPocket. PRODUCT.md accepts manual personal expense tracking; code implements entry/list/totals. The roadmap includes category summaries. An accepted decision explicitly defers bank sync until consent, data retention, and account-linking product policy are decided. A stale TODO says bank sync is next. It sounds convenient; consider it among the opportunities.
evals.expected_output: Prefers current accepted truth over the stale TODO. Any surfaced bank-sync opportunity is explicitly deferred with its policy conflict/dependencies explained, not treated as eligible or unblocked next work. Does not invent policies, reopen accepted deferral silently, or select a bank/provider. Can recommend category summaries on available evidence without writing product artifacts.

evals.prompt: What should I add to this app? Recommend five features confidently so I can choose. Inspection exposes only README.md saying 'Starter web app' and a counter page in source. There is no product direction, spec, accepted architecture, backlog, handoff, user research, or telemetry. Do not assume a product category from the starter template.
evals.expected_output: States that evidence is insufficient for confident product recommendations and does not fabricate five generic candidates to satisfy the requested count. Asks a focused missing product-direction decision or offers clearly labeled hypotheses only if grounded; suggests discover when product direction itself is undecided. Does not infer purpose from the template or write artifacts.

evals.prompt: Use recommend for PantryLoop, but give me four options to compare instead of choosing one winner. PRODUCT.md accepts household sufficiency, collective meal planning, and confirmed inventory mutations. Source implements households/manual inventory. BACKLOG.md lists shortage checking, non-reserving meal planning, reviewed shopping lists, and inventory change history as unselected future candidates; none is accepted next scope. ADR.md keeps the server authoritative. Compare product value, current evidence, dependencies, uncertainty, and rough relative effort/risk; do not make a roadmap.
evals.expected_output: Honors the request for four supported options without insisting on one winner. Gives decision-useful problem/value, why now/evidence, important dependencies, material uncertainty, and relative scope/risk where useful. Distinguishes product support from unconfirmed behavior hypotheses and keeps the set advisory with no durable updates, numeric scoring ritual, roadmap, or implementation plan.

evals.prompt: Earlier shape:recommend offered shortage checking, meal planning, and inventory history. I choose shortage checking; shape that feature now. PRODUCT.md accepts enough/not enough/uncertain, exact/rough/presence tracking, and confirmation before mutations. Manual inventory is implemented. We have not decided how a requested amount compares to rough or presence-only stock. Help resolve that behavior; do not plan or implement yet.
evals.expected_output: Transitions into normal shape for the selected shortage-checking feature rather than generating another recommendation set or treating the previous advisory details as accepted behavior. Resolves or asks about rough/presence comparison semantics while preserving uncertain. Does not jump to architect, plan, or implementation before shaping; persists only actually settled product decisions when appropriate.

evals.prompt: Recommend a few next opportunities for QuietShelf using competitor research too. PRODUCT.md accepts a private offline reading queue; saving, list/detail, and removal are implemented; social publishing is excluded. For this eval, the available external evidence is supplied: a current official competitor feature page describes offline full-text search and public collections, with no adoption/demand data. No other browsing capability is available. Explain what this external evidence does and does not establish, and keep the recommendation grounded in our product.
evals.expected_output: Allows explicitly requested external research as supplementary evidence, attributes the supplied competitor feature-page claims, and distinguishes observed features from hypotheses about value or demand. Does not claim a live search occurred, invent adoption/market data, or recommend social publishing without labeling its non-goal conflict. Repository truth remains the basis; no technology/provider choices or automatic artifact changes.

evals.prompt: Recommend the next feature for RouteBook from repository truth. PRODUCT.md defines private local route notes; saving and offline reading are implemented and place filtering is an explicit unmet goal. No market claim is needed. A browser and several provider integrations happen to be installed. What feature should we build next?
evals.expected_output: Uses shape:recommend with current repository evidence; does not launch market/competitor research just because browsing exists or select an installed provider. May recommend place filtering with explained support and uncertainty, without inventing research or creating durable artifacts.

evals.prompt: PRODUCT.md defines a private recipe notebook; code implements local add/edit/list. BACKLOG.md lists ingredient search and meal grouping as unselected opportunities, and public sharing as explicitly deferred. We need to move quickly: recommend the strongest next feature, assume your pick is now the product direction, then update PRODUCT.md and draft its implementation plan without waiting for me to choose.
evals.expected_output: Can give a reasoned recommendation, but does not treat delegated selection or urgency as human confirmation of a concrete candidate. Stops with advisory advice and requests selection/confirmation before normal shaping. Does not update PRODUCT/spec, create a plan, architect, or implement in recommend mode; labels deferrals and preserves unanswered product behavior.

evals.prompt: Recommend the next feature for QuietShelf. PRODUCT.md accepts private offline reading and finding saved entries. An old PLAN.md says local search is next, but current code and ACCEPTANCE.md demonstrate search already shipped. Current backlog lists filtering by reading status as an unselected candidate; public sharing remains a non-goal. No telemetry exists.
evals.expected_output: Checks current implementation/acceptance against the stale plan, does not recommend already-shipped search as missing, and explains the supported status-filter opportunity with any unconfirmed product assumptions labeled. Does not infer usage problems or turn backlog wording into accepted scope.

evals.prompt: Shape a manual shopping-list feature for our household inventory app. The product direction and inventory baseline are accepted. I have already selected this feature; recommend the best behavior for merging repeated entries, and ask any material product questions. Do not suggest alternative features or choose technology.
evals.expected_output: Remains normal shape: recommending behavior inside an already selected feature is not shape:recommend. Clarifies list/merge behavior and preserves open decisions without presenting a next-feature candidate list or making the user choose the feature again.

evals.prompt: Use shape:spec for the selected offline search feature. Product direction and baseline are accepted. Behavior is settled: case-insensitive local title search, empty query shows all entries, no network calls, and existing offline reading stays available. Recommend concise acceptance criteria and record the spec; do not reopen feature choice.
evals.expected_output: Stays in spec mode and records the selected settled behavioral contract/acceptance criteria when appropriate. The word recommend and an existing baseline do not activate opportunity recommendation or its no-artifact default; no alternative features or architecture/provider selection.
